limits: A rating is ★ coaching over ◆ inputs; the score never gates. The floor (bracket_report.json) is the only bracket gate.
calibrate.py refuses a verdict below 10 decks with 20 games each; no figure here is checked against outcomes yet (`rating --calibrate` reports the refusal with today's n).
Goldfish kill is one column, never the rule: the benchmark is an unopposed ceiling with no blockers and no removal, and a combo or control deck reads slow for not attacking.
Forge is not a power read until the harness work is done (the pilot's rule, 2026-10-18): its component ships at weight 0.00 and is shown only for a run on the current list.
DeckCheck's Threat Index is shown in `context` and never scored.
Diagnostic engine figures are read against each deck's own declaration and are never ranked across decks; they are evidence for the argument, not a component.
rank over n=3 decks; no significance claim

findings.note: validate-rating OK; rating --json re-run matches components, withheld, code_score, bracket, limits exactly.

Says capacity 'reads sound against its cited bands'. The same cited section (interaction-suite) says 'Breadth before depth ... cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land'; the deck's own input audit.interaction-breadth is 3 of 5 classes, and the argument cites only the count (18 in 15-20) and sweepers. The record in rating.json also shows ramp 8 and card-advantage 8, both 'under' their cited ratios (10-12 ramp, 10 draw). 'Sound' omits the breadth shortfall its own source names.
'15- to 20-card interactive suite' is verbatim and is the section's count baseline; 18 answer_cards is inside it.
'one or two max' is the sweeper cap in the section; sweepers=1 satisfies it (the section notes Zupke caps at 3).
skeleton:resilience answer_cards is the real input (18).

50 vs code_score 50.6: claims neither undersell nor oversell; no named figure argues otherwise. Winless 0/5 has Wilson [0,0.4345] spanning par 0.2633, as argued; log hashes 88bffd.../7ce22f.../7be137... all differ from current cbf7fb..., so 'no game logged on it' is true.
engine/diagnosis sha mismatch is not answerable from the skeleton; diagnose settles it.
Log 003 tag one-vampire-cast gives the premise; only a game on the current list settles it.

resolution: the interval spans 0 grade boundaries; measured components carry their inputs' intervals, the judgment none

judgment.argument: The measured components cannot see how this deck plays. Withheld: no surveyed games and no Forge run on the current list, so nothing has shown how the current list behaves at a table. No game is logged on it. The engine write-up and combo proofs were written against an earlier list hash, so I give them no credit. The clock is already scored in speed and the winless record in table_record; I do not deduct for either a second time, and the record's interval is wide enough to include an average result. What is left is capacity, and it reads sound against its cited bands. The deck holds 18 answer cards inside the cited 15- to 20-card interactive suite, and the audit rates its sweeper count at the band, which the strategy caps at one or two max. Nothing in the record or the engine lets me move the number either way: the engine is stale, the games are on older lists, and the measured components already carry the rest. So I land on the middle, where the measured components say it.
